synthesis.description: Michelle Lokay sends the marketing team a recurring Transwestern summary of average deliveries to California, with utilization and San Juan lateral throughput. Alongside it she circulates capacity postings from the EBB for review before they go up and reminds colleagues that bids close at 5:00 on the due date. Colleagues send supporting files such as contract usage of alternate points or the California interstate capacity report, and questions on contract terms or billing are settled by discussion.
steps: Pull the week's delivery volumes to California and San Juan lateral throughput from the pipeline data.
Work out average deliveries and utilization against capacity.
Send the delivery summary to the marketing team.
Draft a capacity posting and ask colleagues to review it before it is published.
Publish the posting on the EBB and circulate the link.
Remind shippers and colleagues of the bid deadline on the due day.
Gather supporting contract or usage files when a capacity question or billing issue comes up.
synthesis.approach: Generate the delivery summary directly from the pipeline's scheduled-volume data: a query fills average deliveries, utilization and lateral throughput into a fixed template, stamps the effective date range automatically, and sends it on a schedule after a quick human check. A posting calendar with automatic bid-deadline reminders would cover the posting and review steps.
synthesis.rationale: The summary repeats the same sentence with new figures each round, so a fixed report layout fed by the data removes the manual calculation and the date errors seen in the mail. Postings and bids still need judgement, which the reminder calendar supports without replacing.
